candidates.name: verbatim_label_memory
candidates.hypothesis: Adding two verbatim-copy instructions to the prompt — (a) copy answer labels character-for-character from the examples, do not paraphrase or add suffixes; (b) include every semicolon-separated label when the answer is multi-label — will outperform symmetric_confusion_memory on tasks with structured label spaces, because trace analysis shows roughly a third of all errors are pure format violations: label-suffix inflation (model appends categorical suffixes not present in training labels) and partial multi-label output (model predicts only the most salient component). Both error classes persist even when the correct label appears in context, so they are prompt-addressable without any change to retrieval.

candidates.name: notation_adaptive_memory
candidates.hypothesis: Extending the tokenizer routing to a three-way strategy — CJK text uses bigrams, ASCII text with >35% non-alphanumeric characters (structured notation such as SMILES, chemical formulae, accession codes) also uses bigrams, and natural-language ASCII uses word tokens — will outperform symmetric_confusion_memory on tasks whose inputs are structured notations, because the existing binary router (CJK→bigram, else→word) extracts only short alphabetic fragments from SMILES strings and loses all structural information encoded in parentheses, brackets, stereo-bond markers, ring closure digits, and bond symbols that distinguish one compound from another.
